clue.text: Webcam I fixed at last for eternal optimist

indicators.note: something fixed has been repaired or rearranged, so these letters are put in a new order
at last points to the final letter of the word that follows it

explanation.surface: Someone repairs a webcam, the last word in hopefulness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' rearranges WEBCAM I into MICAWBE, and 'at last' takes R, the final letter of 'for'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilkins Micawber in Dickens's David Copperfield always believes something will turn up, the model of the incurable optimist.

clue.text: Talos, in UK and Lyon, reading Cider with Rosie?

parts.note: the setter Talos refers to himself, which in English is me
in Lyon, a French city, the setter would say moi, French for me
reading is one of the three Rs, so it gives R

explanation.surface: The setter, at home and in France, is reading Laurie Lee's famous book.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is 'me' in English and 'moi' in French; reading is R, one of the three Rs (reading, writing, arithmetic).
explanation.definitionFit: Laurie Lee's Cider with Rosie is an autobiographical account of his boyhood, an example of life writing.

clue.text: Poetic type of chap in The Police cut Roxanne's outro

indicators.note: cut means the last letter is chopped off the policeman word

parts.note: a copper is a policeman, a man serving in the police

indicators.note: an outro is the closing part of a song, so it means the final letter of Roxanne

explanation.surface: A rock fan muses about a member of the band The Police trimming the ending of their hit Roxanne.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads The Police as the band and Roxanne as their song; 'cut' drops the final R of COPPER, and 'outro' takes E, the last letter of Roxanne.
explanation.definitionFit: François Coppée was a nineteenth-century French poet, a writer of verse.

clue.text: Winner of two Pulitzer prizes with The Colour of Snow and River's Origin

parts.note: snow is white
a river rises at its head, its source

explanation.surface: An author takes literary honours with two books bearing fanciful titles.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make the two pieces look like book titles.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist Colson Whitehead won the Pulitzer Prize for fiction for The Underground Railroad and again for The Nickel Boys.

clue.text: "A numerous host of dreaming saints succeed; / Of the true old breed" (Dryden)

definitions.text: "A numerous host of dreaming saints succeed; / Of the true old breed" (Dryden)

parts.words: A numerous host of dreaming saints succeed; / Of the true old breed" (Dryden)
parts.note: a quotation from Dryden's The Hind and the Panther with one adjective dropped before breed: the solver supplies the missing word describing the zealous saints

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a gap-fill: the missing word belongs between 'old' and 'breed' in Dryden's line.
explanation.definitionFit: Dryden uses the word in its old sense of religious zealots who claim divine inspiration, fitting dreaming saints.

clue.text: "Ace" loads faulty film for Provençal documentarian

indicators.note: loads means one thing is put inside another, so the faulty word takes the ace inside it

parts.note: a dud is something faulty
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
ET is the Spielberg film E.T.

explanation.surface: A dodgy reel of film is loaded for a documentary maker from Provence.
explanation.walkthrough: Ace is A, as on playing cards; the film is Spielberg's E.T.; the solution as printed, GAUDET, is a one-letter slip for the writer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Alphonse Daudet chronicled Provençal life in Letters from My Windmill, recording the region's people and customs.

clue.text: I caught a graduate lifting bio-fuelled calculators

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting means the string of pieces is read from bottom to top

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: Someone says they caught a graduate stealing calculators that run on biofuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' turns the whole string ICABA upwards, giving ABACI.
explanation.definitionFit: Abaci are counting frames moved by hand, so the only power they need is human muscle.

clue.text: Ragtime composer in fix with Loewe on occasion

parts.note: to doctor something is to fix or tamper with it

indicators.note: on occasion means only every other letter of the name Loewe is taken

explanation.surface: A Ragtime composer is in a fix with Frederick Loewe, the Broadway composer, now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on occasion' picks O and W, the second and fourth letters of Loewe.
explanation.definitionFit: E. L. Doctorow wrote the novel Ragtime; 'composer' here means the writer who composed it, not a musician.

clue.text: Trotsky and Lenin? Leaders drinking up inferior red?

indicators.note: drinking means the pair of initials takes something inside them
leaders means the first letters of the two revolutionaries' names
in a down clue, up means the word for inferior is read bottom to top

parts.note: lesser means inferior

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the leading Bolsheviks drank cheap red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' gives T and L, which by 'drinking' take in RESSEL ('up' turning LESSER).
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Tressell, author of The Ragged Trousered Philanthropists, was a committed socialist, a red in political slang.

clue.text: Euro-politician greeting saint and old devil

parts.note: an MEP is a Member of the European Parliament
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A Euro-politician greets a saint and an old devil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old devil' reads as one phrase, but 'old' gives the final O and 'devil' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mephisto, short for Mephistopheles, is the fiend to whom Faust sells his soul in the legend.

clue.text: Detective firm in Kent fronted by old man

indicators.note: fronted by means the next piece goes at the front of the word

parts.note: pa, like old man, is an informal word for father

indicators.note: in means the firm abbreviation sits inside the Kent abbreviation

parts.note: Kent is in the South East of England, abbreviated SE
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A detective firm based in Kent is run by an old man.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in South East England, hence SE; Peter Pascoe is a detective in Reginald Hill's novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Pascoe is the police detective partnered with Andy Dalziel in Reginald Hill's crime novels.

clue.text: Doctor cures palm rot in sickly French author

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A physician treats a palm disease affecting a sickly French writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a medic treating the rot; it is the anagram signal on CURES PALM ROT.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcel Proust, author of In Search of Lost Time, suffered severe asthma and spent years confined to bed.

clue.text: Anger shown by nurse over work of Johnson

parts.note: ire means anger

indicators.note: over means the nurse abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: EN is an Enrolled Nurse

explanation.surface: A nurse shows anger over the writings of Dr Johnson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the nurse round: an Enrolled Nurse (EN) is a British nursing grade. Johnson's only play is far less known than his Dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is the verse tragedy Samuel Johnson wrote, staged by Garrick in 1749.

clue.text: "- they all commit the care And management of this main enterprise" (Milton)

definitions.text: "- they all commit the care And management of this main enterprise" (Milton)

parts.words: they all commit the care And management of this main enterprise" (Milton)
parts.note: a line from Milton's Paradise Regained with its opening word replaced by a dash, which the solver supplies: a word saying everyone agreed together

explanation.walkthrough: The dash marks the missing first word of Milton's line in Paradise Regained.
explanation.definitionFit: The devils in council agree together with no dissent before handing the task to Satan.

clue.text: Detective gets vehicle list for Mr Dodgson

parts.note: Inspector Lewis is a TV detective, Morse's sidekick
a car is a vehicle
a roll is a list of names

explanation.surface: A detective acquires a car and a register of names.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis is Inspector Morse's sergeant and later star of his own British TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lutwidge Dodgson wrote the Alice books under a pen name.

clue.text: Rude moans put off shepherdess with royal background

indicators.note: put off suggests the letters are disturbed and set in a different order

explanation.surface: Coarse groans upset a shepherdess of noble birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put off' rearranges RUDE MOANS.
explanation.definitionFit: In the play for which Schubert wrote music, Rosamunde, Princess of Cyprus, is raised as a shepherdess before her royal birth is revealed.

clue.text: Piece I'm getting edited about daughter in The Plague?

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the daughter abbreviation
edited means the letters have been revised into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An editor revises a piece about a daughter in Camus's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edited' rearranges the first two words into EPIEMIC and 'about' wraps that round D. The question mark flags that Camus's novel only exemplifies the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Camus's The Plague depicts an outbreak sweeping the city of Oran, a disease spreading through a population.

clue.text: Slim men I see texting with three short syllables

clue.text: Dancing a pas de trois around lake is epic!

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the lake abbreviation
dancing suggests the letters move about into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A ballet trio dances round a lake in a performance called epic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dancing' and 'around' both work on the ballet picture; the lake suggests Swan Lake, but it simply gives the letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's Paradise Lost is the great English epic poem of the Fall.

clue.text: Modern artist hack's written about again

indicators.note: written about means the hack word is written round the again word

parts.note: to hack is to cut
bis, from Latin, means twice or again, as a call for a repeat

explanation.surface: A journalist's piece is written up once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hack' looks like a journalist, but it means to chop; bis is the call for a repeat at a concert, from Latin for twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubism, led by Picasso and Braque, was a founding movement of modern art.

clue.text: One who arranged internet service around Spain

indicators.note: around means those two pieces sit either side of the Spain abbreviation

parts.note: the web is the internet
the RN, Royal Navy, is one of the armed services
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A web provider sets up connections around Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' has the first two pieces sitting either side of the Spain letter, not circling it as one word. Spain's international vehicle code is E.
explanation.definitionFit: Anton Webern made famous orchestral arrangements, notably of Bach's Ricercar from The Musical Offering.

clue.text: Outside university, I murder a poor Trilby maker

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters surround the university abbreviation
poor suggests a bad, jumbled version of the letters

explanation.surface: A confession of a feeble murder outside a university, by a hatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges I MURDER A and 'Outside' wraps it round U. Trilby looks like the hat but is the novel.
explanation.definitionFit: George du Maurier wrote the novel Trilby, from whose stage version the trilby hat took its name.

clue.text: Legendary royal is something else, dumping love for you

indicators.note: dumping love for you means the zero-like love letter is replaced by the letter that sounds like you

parts.note: other means something else

explanation.surface: A legendary king is something else, dropping his lover for another.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O (zero in tennis) and 'you' is U in text-speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Uther Pendragon is the father of King Arthur in Arthurian legend.

clue.text: Reepicheep is one river that passes by motorway

indicators.note: passes by means the river comes alongside the motorway letter

parts.note: M stands for motorway, as in the M1
the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A river that flows past a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: Reepicheep is the valiant talking mouse of C. S. Lewis's Narnia books.
explanation.definitionFit: Reepicheep is a talking rodent, an example of the creature.

clue.text: Seedy solipsist knocked back liquor by pub close to bay

indicators.note: knocked back means the liquor word is turned backwards, as if downed

parts.note: rum is a liquor
PH is the abbreviation for public house

indicators.note: close to means the last letter of bay

explanation.surface: A shabby self-absorbed man downs drink in a pub near the bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' turns RUM into MUR; PH is public house, and 'close to' gives Y from bay.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Beckett's Murphy is a down-at-heel hero absorbed in his own mind.

clue.text: Overcook small fish for chap who wrote Feast Days?

parts.note: to burn food is to overcook it
an ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A cook burns a little fish before a feast.
explanation.definitionFit: John Burnside, the Scottish poet and novelist, published the poetry collection Feast Days in 1992.

clue.text: Ancient writer found in cryogenic ice rooms

indicators.note: found in means the answer is sitting within the letters of the next words

explanation.surface: An ancient writer is discovered in freezer rooms, preserved.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through cryogeniC ICE ROoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Cicero was a Roman orator, statesman and prolific author of letters and treatises.

clue.text: Articles by Republican heavyweight Frank Lin?

parts.note: a and the are the two English articles
a ton is a heavy weight

explanation.surface: Pieces by a Republican heavyweight named Frank Lin.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank Lin was the pen name under which Gertrude Atherton published her first novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Californian novelist Gertrude Atherton used Frank Lin as a pseudonym early in her career.
